title: Dual-stage adjudication and temperature-normalized scoring for config rollouts
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: As we expand automated rollouts for model/config changes, small metric deltas from evaluator sensitivity and sampling noise are triggering false alerts or masking regressions. Existing rubrics and LLM-as-judge runs are sensitive to generation temperature, prompt phrasing, and cohort composition. Proposal: implement a dual-stage adjudication (LLM-as-judge primary, targeted human spot-check secondary) combined with temperature-normalized scoring and synthetic perturbation stress tests. This will produce a more robust delta signal tied to config changes, reduce false positives in regression alerts, and enable automated rollback thresholds for high-severity failures. The approach emphasizes per-cohort baselines, calibration layers that map judge scores across sampling temperatures, and an isolated stress harness that simulates distribution shifts tied to config changes (e.g., quantization, context window limits, kernel fallbacks).
acceptance_criteria: LLM-as-judge pipeline returns temperature-normalized scores with documented mapping function across T=0.0..1.0
Human spot-check workflow integrated for any regression > threshold and covers at least 50 randomly selected examples from affected cohorts
Automated rollback trigger implemented: if calibrated delta exceeds X sigma on high-priority cohorts and human spot-check confirms negative signal
Dashboard shows per-config, per-cohort delta, sample-level attribution, and judge confidence percentiles
Synthetic perturbation suite runs as part of PR gating for config changes and reports expected sensitivity metrics
success_metrics: Reduction of false positive regression alerts by >= 60% in first 90 days
Time-to-detection for true regressions stays <= 24 hours
Human review rate for flagged regressions <= 15% of alerted incidents after calibration
Precision of regression alerts (confirmed negative by human) >= 0.8 for P0/P1 features
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 sprints): Design mapping for temperature-normalized judge scores; implement score rescaling service and add storage of judge temperature metadata
Phase 2 (2 sprints): Build synthetic perturbation harness (quantization noise, truncated contexts, kernel fallback traces); integrate into CI for config PRs
Phase 3 (2 sprints): Human spot-check tool and workflow + dashboard panels for per-cohort signal and sample drilldown
Phase 4 (1 sprint): Rollout automated rollback/alert thresholds with canary policy and monitoring for false positives
Ongoing: periodic recalibration cadence (monthly) and rubric refresh synced to model onboarding
milestones: 2026-03-14: Judge rescaling service deployed to staging
2026-04-12: Canary rollout with rollback triggers enabled
stakeholders: Eng: Arjun Patel (owner), Priya Rao (runtime), Lucas Miller (console)
Design: Elena Voss (UX for review flows)
risks: LLM-as-judge drift: judge model updates could change scoring mapping and require frequent recalibration
Human review throughput: spot-checks could become a bottleneck if alert volume spikes
Synthetic stress coverage: harness might miss some real-world failure modes (ops/infra-induced regressions)
False sense of security: over-normalization might hide legitimate context-sensitive regressions
